name: Phoenicians
also_known_as: Sidonians and Tyrians (the Bible's usual names)
summary: The seafaring Canaanites of Tyre and Sidon on the Lebanese coast. They were traders and colonisers across the whole Mediterranean, spread the alphabet, and made the famous purple dye. Hiram of Tyre supplied cedar and craftsmen for Solomon's Temple. Jezebel of Sidon brought Baal worship into Israel. Jesus ministered in the region of Tyre and Sidon.
name_meaning: 'Phoenician' is Greek (Phoinikes), probably from phoinix, 'purple-red', after their dye. They called themselves Canaanites, or by their city: Sidonians, Tyrians.

origin.account: Sidon was Canaan's firstborn son, and the border of the Canaanites began at Sidon. Tyre, 'the strong city', is first mentioned in Joshua. Historically Byblos (Gebal), Sidon, Tyre and Arvad were Bronze Age Canaanite ports that flourished as independent Phoenician city-states after about 1200 BC.

lineage.notes: The Arvadite (Arvad) and Giblites (Gebal/Byblos) are also Phoenician cities in the Bible. Genetic study shows substantial continuity from Bronze Age Sidon to present-day Lebanese.

homeland.region: Phoenicia — the narrow coast of Lebanon between the mountains and the sea
homeland.description: Island and harbour cities backed by the cedar forests of Lebanon, with little farmland — so the Phoenicians turned to the sea. They founded colonies across the Mediterranean, including Carthage (traditionally 814 BC), Cadiz (Tarshish is often linked with Spain), Sicily, Sardinia and Cyprus.
homeland.modern_location: Coastal Lebanon and parts of northern Israel and Syria; colonies in Tunisia, Spain, Sicily, Sardinia and Cyprus.

places.name: Tyre (Tyrus)
places.note: Island city of merchants; besieged by Nebuchadnezzar and taken by Alexander.

places.name: Sidon (Zidon)
places.note: 'Great Zidon'; Paul's friends there cared for him.

places.name: Gebal (Byblos)
places.note: Its craftsmen helped build the Temple; the word 'Bible' comes from its name.

places.name: Zarephath
places.note: Where Elijah was fed by a widow and raised her son.

places.name: Carthage
places.note: Tyre's greatest colony (not named in the Bible).

timeline.event: Sidon marks Asher's border; Asher does not drive out the Sidonians.
Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar, carpenters and masons to build David's house and later Solomon's Temple, and joins Solomon's fleet to Ophir.
Huram, a Tyrian bronze-worker with an Israelite mother, casts the Temple pillars Jachin and Boaz.
Ahab marries Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and serves Baal.
Elijah is sent to a widow of Zarephath; the meal and oil do not fail.
Amos condemns Tyre for selling captives to Edom and forgetting 'the brotherly covenant'.
Nebuchadnezzar besieges Tyre for thirteen years.
Alexander the Great builds a causeway to island Tyre and destroys it after a seven-month siege — as Ezekiel had said, 'thou shalt be a place to spread nets upon'.
Crowds from Tyre and Sidon come to Jesus; he heals the daughter of a Syrophenician woman.
Paul spends seven days with disciples at Tyre and visits friends at Sidon.

religion.practices: Baal and Astarte worship, spread into Israel by Jezebel, who fed 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of the groves at her table. The Carthaginian colony became notorious for child sacrifice (the 'tophet'). Solomon built a high place for Ashtoreth.

importance: Tyre and Sidon show both blessing and danger from outside. Tyrian skill and cedar built the Temple of God. A Sidonian princess, Jezebel, nearly destroyed Israel's faith and provoked the contest on Mount Carmel. Tyre's pride and trade are the subject of Ezekiel's great lament (chs. 26–28), often linked with the fall of Satan. Jesus said that if his mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon 'they would have repented long ago', and a Gentile mother from there won his praise.

impact.how: Built with Tyrian materials, craftsmen and a bronze-worker of mixed Tyrian–Israelite birth.
Hid in Sidonian Zarephath from Jezebel's husband, and was fed by a Gentile widow.
Jezebel's influence led to the killing of the LORD's prophets and the murder of Naboth.
Her answer — 'yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs' — won her daughter's healing.

notable_people.name: Ethbaal
notable_people.role: King of the Zidonians, Jezebel's father

notable_people.name: Jezebel
notable_people.role: Queen of Israel who promoted Baal

notable_people.name: The widow of Zarephath
notable_people.role: Fed Elijah; her son was raised

key_verses.text: Now therefore command thou that they hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon; and my servants shall be with thy servants: and unto thee will I give hire for thy servants according to all that thou shalt appoint: for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.

And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.
And say unto Tyrus, O thou that art situate at the entry of the sea, which art a merchant of the people for many isles, Thus saith the Lord GOD; O Tyrus, thou hast said, I am of perfect beauty.
Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.

fate.summary: The Phoenician cities passed under Assyria, Babylon and Persia, and lost independence after Alexander. They were Hellenised and later Romanised, and became early Christian centres. Carthage fell to Rome in 146 BC, but its Punic language was still spoken in North Africa in Augustine's day (5th century AD).

today.summary: The Phoenicians are the ancestors of much of the population of modern Lebanon. A 2017 genetic study found that present-day Lebanese derive about 93% of their ancestry from the Bronze Age population of Sidon. Tyre (Sour) and Sidon (Saida) are still Lebanese cities; Tyre's ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage site.
today.descendants: Lebanese people in particular, and other coastal Levantine populations.
today.modern_legacy: The Phoenician alphabet is the ancestor of the Greek, Latin, Hebrew and Arabic scripts. 'Bible' derives from Byblos, the Phoenician port through which Egyptian papyrus reached Greece.

archaeology.name: Ahiram sarcophagus
archaeology.significance: Carries one of the earliest fully developed Phoenician alphabetic inscriptions.

archaeology.name: Eshmunazar II sarcophagus
archaeology.significance: Long royal inscription of a king of Sidon.

archaeology.name: Tophet of Carthage (Salammbo)
archaeology.significance: Cemetery of cremated infants and stelae, central to debates about Phoenician child sacrifice.
